translations.text: Thus says Cyrus, king of Persia: The Lord, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has commanded me to make and build him a temple in Jerusalem in Judea.
Cyrus, king of Persia, had all these brought out through Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them and handed them over to Sheshbazzar, the governor of Judah.
The descendants of Bani: one thousand forty-eight.
The descendants of Gidgon, Lod, Hadid, and Ono: seven hundred twenty-five.
The Levites, the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, from the descendants of Hodaviah: seventy-four.
The descendants of Hagab, the descendants of Shalmai, the descendants of Hanan.

And among the descendants of the priests: the descendants of Habaiah, the descendants of Hakkoz, and the descendants of Barzillai. They had taken wives from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and their names were forgotten.

Many of the priests, Levites, and heads of ancestral families—the elders who had seen the temple of the Lord—now saw its foundation with their own eyes and wept loudly. But all the people expressed their joy and raised their voices.
Those who oppressed Judah and Benjamin heard that the Israelites who had come out of captivity were building the house of the Lord, the God of Israel.

Rehum Baal-teem and Shimshai the scribe, and our other fellow servants: the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Okueans [?], the Babylonians, the people of Susa, and [?].

Mighty and powerful kings have ruled in Jerusalem, forcibly holding the western region beyond the Euphrates River. Now impose taxes and tribute on them, so that they may no longer exercise power as they please.

Then the tax collector of King Arsasas, that is, Artaxerxes, brought the letter and read it before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and his fellow servants. They hurried to Jerusalem and Judea with a great force and cavalry, and prevented and stopped the Jews from building.
And this is what Tattenai, governor of the regions of the River, wrote.

May God, whose name dwells there, go forth and devastate the kingdom and the people that dared to stretch out their hand to obstruct and destroy the house of God in Jerusalem. I, King Darius, have issued this decree, and let no one dare to violate it.

Everything that I commanded concerning the house of the Lord, the God of heaven and earth, shall be done. Let no one undertake to obstruct the house of the Lord, the God of Israel, lest wrath come from the Lord God upon my kingdom and my son.

All who do not know, and all who do not act according to the laws of the Lord and the laws of the king, shall be handed over for judgment according to their deeds, whether to death, punishment, fines, or imprisonment.

We arose and departed from the river Eos on the twelfth day of the first month, and came to Jerusalem. The hand of the Lord our God was with us, and he delivered us from the hands of our enemies and from those who attacked us along the road.
For they and their sons took wives from their daughters, and their holy offspring became mingled with the people of that land and were defiled. This lawlessness began with the leaders.
At the evening sacrifice I rose from my distress and, with my clothes torn, bowed down on my knees and spread out and lifted my hands to the Lord God.
And now, what answer shall we give before you, Lord, concerning all this? For we have transgressed your laws, Lord.

And now let us make a covenant before the Lord our God to send away all the foreign wives and the children born to them. And now, as you wish, arise and put these things into effect according to the laws of the Lord God and as the commandments direct.
Then Ezra arose and made the leaders of the priestly and Levitical clans and all Israel swear to act according to this form of oath.
And from the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattha, Bezalel, Binnui, Manasseh.
Mattathias, Zarath, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, Shimei.
